title: Understanding Layers in Photoshop - Day 4
summary: PHLEARN's Day 4 core lesson explains why layers are the backbone of non-destructive editing in Photoshop, covering standard layers, adjustment layers, and special layers such as text and shape layers. The video demonstrates building a photo composite by importing a second image as a new layer, adjusting opacity and visibility, and converting a background layer into a regular editable layer. It introduces Smart Objects for nondestructive editing, shows how to create and edit layer masks from selections, and explains the relationship between layers and masks (including unlinking and relinking). The tutorial then guides edge refinement with Select and Mask, the use of clipping masks for effects like light leaks, painting details with brushes to simulate Polaroid edges, and color grading with a gradient map. Finally, it demonstrates applying Gaussian blur and noise to sell realism, all within a fully non-destructive workflow that preserves the original background.

sections.title: Introduction to Layers and Non-Destructive Editing
concepts: Layers as non-destructive editing foundations
Layer types: standard, adjustment, text/shape
Overview of photo composites using layers and masking
sections.description: The video opens with the case for layers as Photoshop's core tool for non-destructive edits, outlines the different layer types, and previews building a photo composite using layering and masking. It also mentions that sample assets are available for download.

sections.title: Importing a Second Image as a New Layer and Basic Layer Handling
concepts: Drag-and-drop import of an additional image as a new layer
Viewing and toggling layer visibility
Opacity adjustments and the effect on perception
Background layer locking and converting background to a regular layer
sections.description: The presenter drags a second photograph into the document, shows the new layer in the Layers panel, demonstrates opacity control, and explains how the background layer is locked by default and how to convert it to a movable regular layer.

sections.title: Smart Objects, Layer Masks, and Independent Editing
concepts: Smart Object indicators in the Layers panel
Using selections to create layer masks
Making selections independent of the active layer
Converting selections into masks to reveal specific areas
sections.description: The session introduces Smart Objects as a nondestructive editing option, explains making a selection with the Quick Selection Tool, and demonstrates turning that selection into a layer mask on a target layer, while noting that selections can be reused on other layers.

sections.title: Edge Refinement with Select and Mask and Mask-focused Workflows
concepts: Layer vs. layer mask editing (independent controls)
Edge refinement using Select and Mask (feather, contrast, edge shift)
Converting a selection into a mask to refine edges
sections.description: This section clarifies the distinction between editing layers and their masks, demonstrates accessing Select and Mask for feathering and edge refinements, and previews adjusting mask edges for realism.

sections.title: Adding a Light Leak Layer and Color Grading with Clipping Masks
concepts: Importing a light-leak layer as a new, smart object layer
Changing blend modes (e.g., Soft Light) and transforming the light-leak layer
Clipping the light-leak layer to the subject using clipping masks
Alternative: duplicating masks to restrict effects
sections.description: A second image (light leak) is introduced and blended to create atmosphere. The instructor demonstrates clipping the light-leak layer to the subject so the effect is visible only where intended, and discusses options for restricting or duplicating masks to refine the look.

sections.title: Polaroid Edge Finishing with Brush Work and Layering
concepts: Creating a new layer above the subject for painting
Brush tool settings (opacity, flow) and color sampling
Painting darker and lighter areas to simulate Polaroid edges
sections.description: The instructor adds a small layer above the subject, uses a brush with the Paint tool to subtly darken and highlight edges, and explains that the strokes should be uneven to mimic Polaroid exposure characteristics.

sections.title: Color Grading with Gradient Map and Non-Destructive Adjustments
concepts: Gradient Map adjustment layer for color grading
Clipping the gradient map to the subject
Adjusting gradient colors and layer opacity for mood
Revisiting the non-destructive nature of these edits
sections.description: Gradient Map is introduced as a color-grading tool clipped to the subject. The colors can be edited via the gradient editor, and the adjustment layer's opacity can be tuned to achieve the desired look without altering the background.

sections.title: Outro and Recap
concepts: Non-destructive editing is central
Layers can be toggled on/off and adjusted without touching the background
Previewing the full workflow and encouraging practice
sections.description: The host wraps up, reiterating that all changes are non-destructive, the background remains untouched, and inviting viewers to continue following the 30-day Photoshop series.
